messages.author: c83674abdeb15570
messages.subject: LCGM
parts:
Wondering if using create.Models it is possible to generate a series of input scripts for sequential LCGM's that order as:

Intercept only
Linear
Quadratic

Obviously the time scores will differ for the later two, so wasn't sure if this could be 'batched' by using create.Models like LCA where the # of classes gets changed in successive runs. That said, in LCA the numeric specifier is the only value changed whereas here you are actually adding new variables for the latent linear + quadratic slopes.

Thanks for any insight.

Best regards,
J.D.

messages.author: 644e1c01c3c42210
messages.subject: Re: LCGM
parts:
Hi J.D.,

Sure, this should be straightforward. I would just treat the intercept, linear, and quadratic as separate models and use conditional tags to handle the alternatives. Something like the below should work. If you have multiple outcomes, you'd just want to loop over those separately with an outcome iterator (so a nested loop). Attached is an example along these lines.

Best,
Michael

[[init]]
iterators = model;
model=1:3;
modelnames#model = Int Lin Quad;
title#model = "Intercept Only"
"Linear Slope"
"Linear + Quadratic";

t0 = 0;
t1 = 1;
t2#model = 2 2 4;
t3#model = 3 3 9;

filename = "[[modelnames#model]].inp";
outputDirectory = latent_growth_example;
[[/init]]

TITLE: [[title#model]]
DATA:   FILE = "../lcm_data.dat";
VARIABLE: NAMES = y1-y4; MISSING=.;

ANALYSIS:
TYPE=GENERAL;
ESTIMATOR=MLR;

MODEL:
[[model==1]]
i | y1@[[t0]] y2@[[t1]] y3@[[t2#model]] y4@[[t3#model]];
[[/model==1]]

[[model > 1]]
i s | y1@[[t0]] y2@[[t1]] y3@[[t2#model]] y4@[[t3#model]];
[[/model > 1]]

OUTPUT: TECH1 TECH8;
PLOT: TYPE=PLOT3;

messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] Re: LCGM
parts:
Hi J.D.,

Yes, I think you could specify the factor loadings yourself instead of using Mplus growth language. In that case, you might just block the intercepts, linear factors, and quadratic factors and do something like [[model > 1]] Linear stuff here [[/model > 1]] [[model > 2]] Quadratic stuff here [[/model > 2]]. That way the models build up in terms of their syntax in the way you expect.

Cheers,
Michael
